beats.beat: A B Infrabuild operates in two segments: infrastructure creation (railways, bridges, roads) and operating a Ready Mix Concrete (RMC) plant at Kashimira, Thane.

Contracts are won through a competitive tender process: clients float tenders, pre-bid meetings are held, and the contract is awarded to the lowest bidder. The company must deposit a performance guarantee.
Revenue is heavily concentrated: the top few customers accounted for 57% of total revenue in FY2018, and Western Railway alone made up 52% of the order book.
The company uses the 'Box Pushing' technique for construction, and relies on state-of-the-art machinery and quality control systems at its RMC facility.
Operations are geographically concentrated in Mumbai and Maharashtra, which the filing acknowledges as a dependency risk.

beats.beat: Revenue from operations has declined from ₹90.21 crore in FY2015 to ₹60.53 crore in FY2018, a drop of about 33% over three years.
Net profit after adjustments was volatile: ₹95.95 lakhs in FY2014, fell to ₹15.86 lakhs in FY2017, then jumped to ₹314.66 lakhs in FY2018.
EBITDA (Profit Before Interest, Depreciation and Tax) ranged from ₹6.76 crore in FY2017 to ₹9.46 crore in FY2015, with FY2018 at ₹9.29 crore.
Long-term borrowings were reduced from ₹6.73 crore in FY2015 to ₹1.33 crore in FY2018, but short-term borrowings increased from ₹30.82 crore to ₹35.37 crore over the same period.
Total assets grew from ₹70.62 crore in FY2014 to ₹82.32 crore in FY2018, indicating working capital expansion.
The company reported negative cash flows from operations in recent financial years, which the filing flags as a risk.

financials.heading: Financial Performance

beats.beat: Amit Bholanath Mishra is the sole promoter, holding 74,95,476 equity shares — 90.949% of the pre-issue capital. Other directors (Bharat Parmar, Shree Prakash Singh, Mukesh Pandey) hold only 300 shares each.
Key management personnel include Anchal Pachori (CFO, CA) and Mohit Soni (Company Secretary, ACS). Hatim Sakerwala holds 9% of equity shares.
Related-party transactions in FY2018 include loans taken from KMP/Board of Directors of ₹68.4 lakhs, director remuneration of ₹57.7 lakhs, and outstanding payables of ₹324.3 lakhs.
Two companies promoted by the promoter — Al-Noor Chickens Private Limited and A B Magma Automobiles Private Limited — were struck off by the ROC in March 2016 due to non-operation.
The company issued equity shares in the last 12 months at a price lower than the issue price (exact price not disclosed). There is no independent appraisal or monitoring agency for the IPO.

beats.beat: The infrastructure sector includes power, bridges, dams, roads, and urban development. It contributes about 8% to India's GDP and is highly fragmented and working-capital intensive.

India requires an estimated investment of ₹50 trillion (US$777.73 billion) in infrastructure by 2022. The logistics sector is expected to grow at 10.5% CAGR from US$160 billion in 2017 to US$215 billion by 2020.
Key demand drivers include government flagship programs (Smart Cities, AMRUT, Make in India, Power for All), eased FDI norms in 15 sectors, and rising urbanization and disposable income.
Headwinds identified by the company include slow pace of government projects, working capital crunches, and changes in government policies.
Competition comes from both organized and unorganized players. The filing does not name specific competitors.

beats.beat: A B Infrabuild Limited builds infrastructure and runs a ready-mix concrete plant, primarily in Mumbai and Maharashtra. It is an SME IPO on the SME Board.
The company's major clients include Western Railway, Central Railway, MCGM, MMRDA — with Western Railway alone contributing 57% of revenue in FY2018.
The IPO consists of 44,28,000 fresh equity shares of ₹10 each, with the price to be determined. Proceeds will primarily fund working capital.

intro.purpose: Orient the reader: A B Infrabuild is a Mumbai-based infrastructure construction and RMC company, seeking to raise funds via an SME IPO.

beats.beat: The issue comprises 44,28,000 equity shares of ₹10 each, entirely a fresh issue. The price band will be determined later.
Proceeds from the fresh issue will be used to meet working capital requirements (₹1,130 lakhs) and for general corporate purposes (amount not disclosed).
The lead manager is Mark Corporate Advisors Private Limited, and the registrar is Bigshare Services Private Limited.
The company has not appointed any independent agency for project appraisal or a monitoring agency for fund deployment. The audit committee will monitor usage.

beats.beat: Customer concentration: Indian Railways (Western Railway) contributed 57% of revenue in FY2018. Losing this client would significantly impact revenue.
Business depends on winning government tenders. If bids are not accepted or are awarded at lower values, revenues would be adversely affected.
Negative cash flows in recent years: sustained negative cash flow could strain operations and financial condition.
Geographic concentration: most revenue comes from Mumbai and Maharashtra. Any adverse development in these regions could hurt results.

These ratios improved sharply from FY2017 (EPS ₹0.63, NAV ₹44.71? check) but the filing shows NAV per share for FY2018 as ₹44.71, and for FY2017 as ₹[?] … Actually from facts: FY2017 EPS 0.63, RoNW 1.97%; FY2016 EPS 1.31, RoNW 4.14%. The DRHP includes a comparison with peer group companies, but the digest does not list the peers or their ratios.
